reason: Signals S1+S3+S4+S5a fire: 'Telephone Boxes' maps to two commercially and structurally incompatible product families — telecom cable distribution enclosures (MDF/DP/Krone boxes, bought by telecom contractors and BSNL/MTNL operators) and prefabricated telephone booth kiosks (FRP/steel walk-in structures, bought by municipal bodies and construction firms) — with zero shared buyer profile, incompatible procurement channels, and incompatible regulatory regimes (TEC/IP-rating telecom standards vs. civil/prefabricated structure norms).

The taxonomy placement under 'Prefabricated Structures' with parent 'Telephone Booths' further confirms structural misalignment: the dominant commercial segment (distribution boxes, 288 listings) belongs in telecom infrastructure, not civil construction, reinforcing that the MCAT name attracts incompatible buyer intents simultaneously.
